text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Nation mourns and buries its dead. Israeli army casualties are highest in one day since 1973 Yom Kippur War.
- Inquiry panel begins its task.
- Tears for 73 families.
- Swiss banks establish Holocaust fund.
- Palestinian Authority blasts plan for Israeli industrial park near Gaza.
- Palestinians down to 0.7 percent of local workforce.
- Call to combine Fruit, Citrus Marketing boards.
- Tecnomatix's net income up 78 percent.
- Profits up 26 percent at British Sky Broadcasting.
GLOBES
- Budget department proposes examining alternatives to an additional 1.5 billion shekel cut.
- Record on stock exchange and in dollar.
HAARETZ
- Inquiry into helicopter collision tends to focus on human error as the cause. Senior official in air force: Pilots hovered over area after not receiving permission to enter Lebanon immediately.
- U.S. helicopter manufacturers offer to send experts to help investigation.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's director-general Avigdor Lieberman investigated in attorney-general affair.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- The 73 boys who did not return.
